protocol.description:
Lets a client be told when the user interacts outside a surface it cares about, so it can dismiss a popup/menu - the "click outside to close" pattern.
Deliberately narrower than a general focus-limiting protocol: one grab always covers exactly one surface (a shell popout is always one layer-shell surface), so there is no whitelist/commit dance - just create, get told when it's cleared, destroy.

interface.name: ironland_focus_grab_manager_v1
interface.description: This interface allows a client to create focus grab objects.

request.name: grab
request.description:
While the returned object is alive, a pointer or touch event outside `surface`, or a key press while `surface` doesn't have keyboard focus, clears the grab: the compositor sends `cleared` and the grab becomes inert (further input outside the surface is not reported again - destroy and re-request to grab again).
Destroying `surface` clears the grab the same way.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the manager doesn't destroy grab objects already created through it.

event.name: cleared
event.description: Sent at most once per object, the first time an outside interaction (or the grabbed surface's destruction) clears the grab.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Ends the grab immediately if it's still active. No `cleared` event is sent for an explicit destroy.
